explorer.clip_note: Each Meshy re-rig has its OWN bone frames (the jump rig's spine is rotated 180° to the idle's), so clips cannot be copied by bone name — the waist folds. scripts/retarget-clip.mjs retargets in world space: per bone, the rotation delta the source clip applies to the source bind pose, applied to the idle rig's bind pose, expressed locally; the spine chain is matched by position (Hips > Spine02 > Spine01 > Spine > neck > Head); hip translation dropped (the body carries height). Clip files are skeleton + rotations only (20–30 KB). Loaded by lib/worldassets.ts loadWorldClips.
explorer.posture_note: The mesh and the ORIGINAL job's rig stand upright (bind pose: pelvis over the feet, spine vertical). The crouch — pelvis tipped forward, knees bent, "as if the pack were heavy" (Selorm) — is in Meshy's 3d_rigging outputs: those re-rig a decimated proxy of the mesh and their canned walk/jump come out crouched on this child-proportioned skeleton even in Meshy's own render. retarget-clip.mjs therefore damps the pelvis and knee deltas (--damp) toward the upright bind while keeping the thigh swing, and adds a small pelvis-pivot lean. No pelvis offset any more; the waist front stays slimmed 32%.
explorer.mesh_edit: scripts/slim-waist.mjs 0.68 0.64 1.0 0.08 — the front of the waist band (hoodie knot + belt pouches) sat 3 cm ahead of the chest; flattened 32% so the chest is the forward-most line of the torso ; scripts/narrow-pelvis.mjs 0.92 0.9 0.55 0.9 — the pelvis band narrowed 8% side-to-side and 10% front-to-back (Selorm: the pelvis dominates the front view)
